name: tenetora
description: Tenetora shared engineering-agent governance with decision alignment, qualified built-in subagent role fallback, and cross-tool runtime adapters.

adapters.notes: Codex plugin manifest exposes all lifecycle skills and Codex-specific runtime hooks, including observation of host-dispatched subagents. Hooks never spawn agents. Non-managed hooks require explicit review in /hooks before they execute.

Claude Code plugin manifest exposes lifecycle skills and runtime hooks for route/rules, alignment recommendations, commit guard, external-input guard, subagent lifecycle observation, and claim-proof enforcement.

The installer writes lifecycle skills plus an auto-loaded JavaScript plugin for session context, compaction context, and pre-tool Git guards. OpenCode has no equivalent enforced Stop hook, so runtime coverage is partial.

Pi uses a global auto-loaded TypeScript extension for session context, prompt context, compaction refresh, and pre-tool Git guards. Project extensions remain gated by Pi project trust. Pi has no verified Tenetora subagent or mandatory Stop contract here, so runtime coverage and delegation remain host-dependent.
The installer merges managed entries into user or project hooks.json without replacing unrelated hooks. Session context, shell Git guards, and bounded stop follow-up are enabled.
ZCode uses a dedicated process-hook manifest with ZCODE_PLUGIN_ROOT, observes recognized host subagent lifecycle events without spawning them, and is installed through its registered plugin cache.
Generic Agents has no shared runtime-hook standard. Lifecycle skills and the CLI remain available, but hook activation must never be inferred from skill installation.

fallback.notes: Tools without a verified runtime-hook adapter install the same lifecycle skills and CLI from the release zip and are reported as skills-only.
